grants.title: Ready To Learn Programming
grants.funder: U.S. Department of Education (Office of Elementary and Secondary Education)
grants.award: $7,000,000 estimated total program funding; typical awards vary by cooperative agreement

contact.programOfficer: Jennifer F. Todd (Grantor); Tammy Proctor (Supervisory Education Program Specialist, 202-260-7803)
contact.notes: Cooperative agreement to develop and disseminate accessible instructional programming (incl. digital content) for preschool and elementary school children. RTL is a national program under Section 2324 of the Every Student Succeeds Act (CFDA 84.346A).

grants.title: NSF Eddie Bernice Johnson INCLUDES (Inclusion across the Nation of Communities of Learners of Underrepresented Discoverers in Engineering and Science)
grants.award: Up to $2,000,000 per award; total program funding varies by track

contact.notes: NSF Big Idea. Supports collaborative networks, alliances, and pilot projects that broaden participation in STEM. Nonprofits and community organizations are eligible as lead or sub-award partners.

grants.title: NSF STEM K-12 (Discovery Research in Formal and Informal Settings)
grants.award: Award sizes vary by track; typical exploratory/standard/full research projects from $300K to $3M over 2-5 years

contact.notes: EDU DRL program: research on STEM teaching and learning in formal/informal settings. Nonprofits may collaborate via subaward or as lead PI with eligible partner. Rolling submission window — confirm current target date on NSF and grants.gov.

grants.title: NSF Advanced Technological Education (ATE)
grants.award: $475,000 to $7,500,000 per award; total program funding varies by track (Planning, Small, Standard, Large, Center)

contact.notes: Primary lead must be a two-year IHE, but explicit partnerships with K-12 schools, industry, and community-based organizations are required. Hacker Dojo could serve as a community/industry partner on a subaward.

grants.title: NSF National Innovation Corps Teams (I-Corps Teams)
grants.award: From $50,000 minimum per award (no fixed ceiling)

contact.notes: Supports small teams to conduct customer discovery and accelerate translation of NSF-funded research into products. Nonprofits that house NSF-funded research teams are eligible. Rolling submission — confirm current window on NSF and grants.gov.

grants.title: Community Connect Grant Program
grants.award: $100,000 to $5,000,000 per award (grant, with 15% match required from non-federal sources)

contact.notes: 7 CFR Part 1739. Funds broadband deployment and community-oriented connectivity projects in rural, economically-challenged communities. Requires a community center with free public broadband access for 2 years. Bay Area applicants should verify whether the specific service area qualifies as rural under the program definition.

grants.title: Section 4 Capacity Building for Community Development and Affordable Housing
grants.funder: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
grants.award: $1,000,000 to $42,000,000 per award (national competition; HUD issues multiple awards)

contact.notes: Strengthens Community Development Corporations (CDCs) and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) to carry out community development activities. Funds can support technology/training capacity. Requires CDC or CHDO designation — Hacker Dojo is not a CDC but could partner with one.

grants.title: U.S.-India Sports Technology Dialogues and Innovation Program
grants.funder: U.S. Mission to India (Department of State)

contact.notes: Only literal 'EdTech' keyword hit on grants.gov. CFDA 19.040. Requires implementing activities tied to the U.S.-India bilateral trade agenda in India. Strong geographic/mission mismatch for a California-based community nonprofit; included only because the keyword 'EdTech' returned this single posting.

evidence.content: Ready To Learn Programming closeDate 07/08/2026 (per grants.gov Search2 API). Archive date Aug 07, 2026; posted May 11, 2026.

Description: 'promote school readiness and academic achievement through the development and dissemination of accessible instructional programming for preschool and elementary school children and their families … develop and disseminate programming and digital content containing Ready to Learn programming that is specially designed for nationwide distribution over public television stations' digital broadcasting channels and the Internet.' Cooperative agreement supports digital content for youth.
Grantor contact: Jennifer F. Todd, Readytolearn@ed.gov, 202-550-1658; Tammy Proctor Supervisory Education Program Specialist 202-260-7803.
NSF INCLUDES closeDate 10/27/2026 (per grants.gov Search2 API).

NSF Big Idea program focused on broadening participation in STEM. Supports collaborative Networks, Alliances, and Pilot Projects — community organizations and nonprofit partners explicitly encouraged to lead or co-lead engagement projects.
Award ceiling $2,000,000 per award, floor $200,000 per award (per fetchOpportunity).

'The NSF STEM K-12 program in the Division of Research on Learning in Formal and Informal Settings (DRL) in the Directorate for STEM Education (EDU) supports fundamental, applied, and translational research that advances STEM teaching and learning … across a range of formal and informal settings.' Open to NSF standard-eligible organizations; nonprofit community partners may apply directly or as subawardee.
Advanced Technological Education closeDate 10/01/2026 (per grants.gov Search2 API).

'With a focus on two-year Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs), the Advanced Technological Education (ATE) program supports the education of technicians for the high-technology fields … The program involves partnerships between academic institutions (grades 7-12, IHEs), industry, and economic development agencies.' ATE is 2-yr IHE led but requires partner organizations including K-12 and community groups.

NSF National I-Corps Teams: supports small teams to conduct customer discovery and accelerate translation of NSF-funded research. Award floor $50,000. Nonprofits that are current NSF awardees or whose research teams are affiliated with NSF-funded research may apply.
Community Connect Grant Program closeDate 06/29/2026 (per grants.gov Search2 API).

'The Community Connect Grant Program provides financial assistance to eligible applicants that will provide service at or above the Broadband Grant Speed (100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up) to all premises in rural, economically-challenged communities where broadband service (10 Mbps down and 1 Mbps up) does not exist … The deployment of broadband services on a community-oriented connectivity basis stimulates economic development and provides enhanced educational and health care opportunities in rural areas.'
HUD Section 4 Capacity Building closeDate 07/06/2026 (per grants.gov Search2 API).

'The program enhances the capacity and ability of Community Development Corporations (CDCs) and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) to carry out community development and affordable housing activities that benefit low-income persons, homeless, physically disabled persons, first responders and veterans.' Eligible applicants are CDCs/CHDOs; technology orgs would partner with a CDC.
U.S.-India Sports Technology Dialogues closeDate 06/20/2026 (per grants.gov Search2 API).

'The U.S. Embassy in New Delhi announces an open competition for organizations to implement the U.S. India Sports Technology Partnership Program … supports Mission 500, the mandate to double bilateral trade between the United States and India to $500 billion by 2030.' Geographic and mission fit is poor for a California community nonprofit; included only because it is the only grants.gov opportunity matching the literal keyword 'EdTech'.

rationale: The literal keyword 'EdTech' on grants.gov returns only ONE posted opportunity (OFOP0002831, U.S.-India Sports Technology Dialogues) and it is a poor geographic/mission fit for a California 501(c)(3) community tech nonprofit serving youth. To expand coverage to plausible EdTech-relevant federal funding, I queried the Search2 API for the closely related themes of STEM, youth technology, community maker, technology education, broadband community, advanced technological education, and innovation corps. I selected 8 currently-posted, non-closed federal grant opportunities with verified close dates (or open rolling submission windows) that a community technology nonprofit serving youth in STEM could plausibly pursue — as a lead applicant, sub-award partner, or via a designated-eligible lead partner. The strongest fits (ED-GRANT-26-055 Ready To Learn, NSF 22-622 INCLUDES, NSF 25-545 STEM K-12, NSF 24-584 ATE) all align with Hacker Dojo's mission of community learning, technology access, and youth STEM engagement. I excluded research-only NSF programs restricted to university PIs (e.g., 23-510 IUSE, 23-595 CREST, 23-586 Noyce) that explicitly require IHE-eligible lead applicants, as well as State Department international exchange programs that require overseas activity. Community Connect and HUD Section 4 are weaker fits but plausibly accessible via partnership. Award ceilings/floors and contact details are pulled from the grants.gov fetchOpportunity API; close dates are from the Search2 API; full opportunity pages are JS SPAs and were not navigable headlessly during this crawl.
